request: Check whether DMG Synth VGM playback is distorted/clipping and whether mixer balancing is applied. Verification only; do not modify the sound or product code.

gainPolicy.defaultSelection: Fallback/factory/saved gain values replace one another; .28 and .36 are not multiplied.

browserFinding.precision: Peaks rounded here; full precision and exact counts are in the meter receipt. Unique counts are per-channel samples, not distinct audible glitch events.
browserFinding.constraints: Normal foreground playback; no deliberate load/stress. All speaker routes were gain zero before app JS. Headless Chromium and WebKit; no OS volume or ordinary browser used.

ruledOut: Native per-channel summation saturation before the JS mixer.
Accidental multiplication of .28 and .36 mixer defaults.
Simple gain doubling in the meter, verified using known Offline stereo signals.
A trivial deterministic small-buffer/resampling-only explanation: synthetic Offline constant controls at both source rates and three segment lengths were normal.
Scheduled buffer late starts, gaps or overlaps in these ordinary-load captures; all were zero by the requested/actual start-time metrics.
unresolved: The exact real-time signal path/scheduling mechanism creating the peaks remains unlocated. Do not describe it as a confirmed resampling bug or fix it by merely lowering gain.
conclusion: Gain balancing is applied. The supplied unchanged VGM is below full scale offline even at Master380%, but real browser playback produces extra transient peaks and over-full-scale PCM at380%. At70%, no over-full-scale samples were recorded, although extra peaks remain. This supports investigating the VGM real-time rendering path before FM2612 rollout.
changes: Investigation artifacts and issue records only. Product JS/CSS/WASM, calibration gains and presets unchanged.
